definition: Latent Consistency Model — a distilled diffusion model that generates images in 2–4 steps instead of dozens, enabling near-real-time image synthesis.
details: Latent Consistency Model — a distilled diffusion model that generates images in 2–4 steps instead of dozens, enabling near-real-time image synthesis.

explainer.lead: A Latent Consistency Model is a distilled diffusion model that produces images in a handful of steps rather than dozens. That makes near-real-time image synthesis practical.

tiers.eli5: Like a shortcut recipe that skips most of the simmering but still gets the dish on the table fast.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers distill a slower diffusion model into an LCM to cut inference steps; a pitfall is that aggressive distillation can cost some image quality or diversity.
tiers.paperLevel: A distilled diffusion model that generates images in 2–4 steps instead of dozens; the trade-off is fewer sampling steps against fidelity to the original model.

explainer.example: An app generates a preview image from a text prompt in a few steps instead of running a full multi-step diffusion process.
